capitals.name: Mbanza Kongo (São Salvador from the late 16th century)
capitals.note: Coordinates from the gazetteer's Mbanza Kongo entry. The page: the capital was renamed São Salvador in the late 16th century and 'reverted to the name M'banza-Kongo in 1975'. The Kongo Civil War page: the city was burnt in 1678 and 'the capital was abandoned for a time'; claimants ruled from mountain fortresses (Kinlaza at Mbula and Kibangu, Kimpanzu at Mbamba Luvota).

capitals.name: São Salvador (Mbanza Kongo)
capitals.note: 'On February 15, 1709 King Pedro marched on São Salvador'; 'King Pedro died in 1718, leaving an at least partially reunified kingdom with its capital back at São Salvador'. Portugal built a fort and garrison there in 1859 (withdrawn 1866).

correction.text: Lukeni lua Nimi 'established a new base on the mountain Mongo dia Kongo' and allied with the Mwene Kabunga whose lands lay west of there

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1440 but the page dates the founding to c. 1390 (infobox 'Conquest of Kabunga: 1390'). The page gives no boundary for the first kingdom, only the capital, so it is drawn as the district around Mbanza Kongo (confidence low).

131,582 km2 against the infobox 129,400 km2 (1623) and the 'core region of some 130,000 square kilometres' of the late 16th century: ratio 1.02. The same polygon is used for 1440-1669, so before Afonso's expansion 'to the south and east' (1509 to the 1540s) it probably over-draws; the page gives no earlier extent. Unverified: page budget.

Matches the 1623 infobox area (129,400 km2, ratio 1.02). The page says the kingdom 'at its greatest extent' reached 'from the Atlantic Ocean in the west to the Kwango River in the east, and from the Congo River in the north to the Kwanza River in the south', which is larger than this shape (bbox 12.2-16.6 E, 8.5-4.3 S); the shape is the core of the late 16th century.

'King Pedro died in 1718, leaving an at least partially reunified kingdom with its capital back at São Salvador'; peace held 'roughly 50 years' and afterwards the kingdom was 'disintegrat[ing] into fiefdoms recognising the King of Kongo' without effective control; 'After 1708, Soyo did not participate at all in the elections' (Soyo page). ledger.note: 1509 onward: Afonso I extends the kingdom. 'Afonso continued to expand the kingdom of Kongo into the 1540s, expanding its borders to the south and east.' The page dates Afonso's accession to the 1509 succession battle but gives no year or place for the conquests; Cliopatria's shape does not change.

ledger.note: 1526: Afonso reconquers the rebel province of Mpanzalumbu. The page dates it but does not say where the province lay, so the region is the Kongo core region at confidence 1.

ledger.note: 1622: Portugal invades Mbamba (Mbumbi). 'First Kongo-Portuguese War ... Portugal invades Mbamba (Mbumbi), and Kongo defeats the Portuguese at Mbanda Kasi in January 1623.' Portuguese Angola belonged to the Spanish crown under the Iberian Union (Cliopatria lists Spanish Empire as the neighbour 1582-1639); the counterpart is the Portuguese Angolan colony (portuguese-angola). The zone is the southern band of the Kongo shape.

ledger.counterpart: Soyo (county of Kongo, then independent Counts and Grand Princes of Soyo)
ledger.note: 1656: Soyo is lost to the crown. 'By the end of Garcia's reign it was independent' (Kongo Civil War page); the Kingdom of Kongo page calls the counts 'the now independent Counts of Soyo' after their 1670 victory over the Portuguese at Kitombo, and the Soyo page: 'Soyo became an independent state in the 17th century'. 1656 is the last failed campaign; the pages give no exact year for the break (confidence 2).

1678: São Salvador is sacked and abandoned. 'resulting in a battle that killed King Daniel I and burnt most of the city to the ground in 1678'; the capital was abandoned for a time and the claimants ruled from mountain fortresses (Mbula and Kibangu for the Kinlaza, Mbamba Luvota for the Kimpanzu).

ledger.note: 1709 February 15: Pedro IV marches on São Salvador and the kingdom is reunified after the civil war of 1665-1709. 'On February 15, 1709 King Pedro marched on São Salvador at the head of his army carrying only a cross' (infobox: 'Reunification: February 1709'). The page gives no territory for the restored kingdom; the old shape without Soyo is used.

1709 February 15: the king re-enters São Salvador, the capital again from 1709. 'King Pedro died in 1718, leaving an at least partially reunified kingdom with its capital back at São Salvador.' Pedro IV later renamed his base São Francisco de Kibangu after his October 1709 victory over João II.

region.text: Kongo, whose king Pedro swore vassalage in 1859: the royal district of São Salvador

ledger.note: 1859: Pedro V swears vassalage to Portugal and the kingdom becomes a titular Portuguese vassal. 'Portugal thus gained nominal authority over Kongo when Pedro gained control of it in 1859'; Portugal built a fort at São Salvador and withdrew its garrison in 1866. The infobox gives 1857 and the lead 1862; the page conflicts. The vassal tint belongs to the suzerain's dossier (portuguese-angola with counterpart kingdom-of-kongo). [Reviewer af-06, 2026-10-19: type changed from rename to vassal_start with counterpart portuguese-angola, the mirror of portuguese-angola's vassal_start of 1859; the page: 'From 1862 to 1914, it functioned intermittently as a vassal state of the Kingdom of Portugal'. The relation lasts to the 1914 dissolve, so no vassal_end]

wars.name: Jaga invasion of Kongo
wars.outcome: Jaga raiders overran the kingdom; Álvaro I's rule begins amid the crisis and he later allows a Portuguese colony in Luanda.
wars.note: The page names the invasion under 1568 and gives no territorial result, so no border change is recorded.

wars.name: First Kongo-Portuguese War

zones.text: Mbamba (Mbumbi), the southern province; the page says only 'Mbamba and Mpemba (south)'

wars.outcome: Portugal invaded Mbamba (Mbumbi); Kongo defeated the Portuguese at Mbanda Kasi in January 1623.
wars.note: The page names the war but does not link an article for it.

wars.name: Kongo campaigns against Soyo
belligerents: Soyo (county of Kongo, then independent Counts and Grand Princes of Soyo)

zones.text: Soyo, which 'stretched south from the mouth of the Congo River to the River Loze, and inland from about 100 kilometers'

wars.outcome: Garcia II's attempts on Soyo in 1641, 1643, 1645 and 1656 all failed; Soyo was independent by the end of his reign.
wars.note: The Kingdom of Kongo page gives 1645 and 1646.

wars.name: Portuguese-Dutch war in Angola (Kongo as Dutch ally)
wars.outcome: The Dutch took Luanda in 1641 and allied with Kongo; Kongo troops helped Queen Nzinga defeat the Portuguese at Kombi in 1647; the Dutch withdrew in 1648 and Portugal held Luanda by 1649.

wars.name: Battle of Mbwila
wars.outcome: Portuguese forces defeated Kongo on 29 October 1665 and King António I was killed; Portugal obtained an act of vassalage from D. Isabel, regent of Mbwila.
wars.note: The page describes no formal territorial settlement; Mbwila was claimed by both Kongo and Angola and Portugal 'was unable to exercise any real authority over the region once their forces had withdrawn'.

wars.name: Kongo Civil War
belligerents: Soyo (county of Kongo, then independent Counts and Grand Princes of Soyo)
wars.outcome: 'The Kongo Civil War (1665-1709)' between the Kinlaza and Kimpanzu houses, with the Água Rosada of Kibangu and the da Silva of Soyo taking part; São Salvador was burnt in 1678 and Pedro IV re-entered it on 15 February 1709; Mbata and Nsundi broke away.
wars.note: The Kingdom of Kongo page calls it 'a 40-year-long civil war'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontier is given by the pages; the kingdom's provinces and frontiers are approximate. The 1885 division (Berlin Conference) is the first partition by European agreement but the page gives no line.

notes: Cliopatria's three shapes are one polygon (131,582 km2) for 1440-1669, which matches the page's late-16th-century core (~130,000 km2). The row ends in 1669 but the page has the kingdom continuing to 1914, so this dossier adds keyframes for 1390-1439 (founding, the Mbanza Kongo district), 1670-1708 (civil war), 1709-1884 (restored kingdom) and 1885-1914 (titular vassal), all at confidence 1 for their extent; a gap-filler should open 'Pedro V of Kongo' and the Kimpanzu-Kinlaza lands. Page budget (1-2 pages) was spent on the state article and the Battle of Mbwila; the Kongo Civil War and Soyo pages were added (found by search; 'Kongolese Civil War' does not exist) because the 1662-1709 keyframes needed them. Soyo needs a dossier (suggested slug county-of-soyo; independent by c. 1656; no page opened dates its end), so the Soyo counterpart is a name, not a slug. The vassal tint 1859-1914 belongs in the portuguese-angola dossier (vassal_start 1859). The Mbanda Kasi, Kitombo and Kombi battles have articles that were not opened. Region names the gazetteer lacks: none; Mbamba is drawn as a polygon band because the page does not locate it. The Mbwila page says the battle changed no border; Nsundi and Mbata broke away during the civil war (undated, unlocated).
